label: third input after an "l l" or "l x" opening
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost always at step t=2 (98% of mass), and only when the sequence opens with l l or l x. On dev it fires at every such step (precision 1.0) whatever the third token is. Magnitude depends on the third input: v gives the maximum (1.0 relative), and other tokens give about 0.2-0.3. Most misses are weak t=2 activations on v after other openings with l or x in them (x l v ~0.47, x x v ~0.32, r l v ~0.01), plus a few weak t=3 activations (e.g. f l x v). Never fires at the delimiter or during copy, never at t=0/1, and not after openings without l/x.

issues: The main claims hold up. The feature fires only in the original phase (0 activations at the delimiter or in copy). By step it is t=2 for 98.3% of mass and t=3 for 1.7%, with nothing at t=0/1. On test the predicate has precision 1.0 (0 false positives), recall 0.926 and F1 0.961.

The magnitude claim holds. When the opening is l l or l x and the third input is v, there are only 36 test steps (3% of active steps) but they carry 11.2% of activation mass. That is about 3-4x the per-step activation of other third tokens.

There is a systematic miss class that the predicate leaves out: an opening of x followed by l or x, with v as the third input. Scored alone, (t==2)&(orig(0)==x)&orig(1) in {l,x}&(in_tok==v) has test precision 1.0, but its 32 steps hold 4.2% of mass, at activations of 0.32-0.47. These make up most of the top-quartile misses: top-quartile coverage of the original predicate is only 0.88.

The explanation says a broader 'v after l/x' clause was rejected because it halved precision. That is true for 'v after any l/x second token', but the narrower x-opening clause has precision 1.0 and raises test F1 from 0.961 to 0.976 and mass recall from 0.943 to 0.985. The rejection was therefore premature.

The residual misses after the fix are also structured, not random. There is weak firing (0.06-0.32) on v at t=3 right after an 'l l' or 'x l' pair (for example 'r l l v', 'h l l v', 'a x l v'), and very weak firing on v at t=2 after r l or o l (around 0.01-0.06). Together they hold 1.5% of mass. Read together, this points to a secondary 'v right after an l/x pair early in the sequence' component that the label leaves out.
skeptic.revised_label: third input after an "l l" or "l x" opening (strongest when that input is v); also fires on v after an "x l" or "x x" opening

final_label: third input after an "l l" or "l x" opening (strongest when that input is v); also fires on v after an "x l" or "x x" opening
